samples.summary: Gate 1b reads the PR's diff against its OWN base branch, so a PR stacked on a branch that already gutted the CI definition passes the gate
samples.evidence: `branchEditsCiDefinition` calls `repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/${number}/files`, which enumerates the diff of head against the PULL REQUEST'S BASE, not against `main`. The gate's stated invariant (mark-ready.mjs:20-29, and the report line at :238 "CI ran main's definition") only holds when base IS the default branch, and nothing in this script or in the promote job checks that: `pr view --json` at :122-128 never fetches `baseRefName`, and grep of scripts/agent finds no base-branch constraint anywhere on the promote path. Concretely: branch A edits `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to remove every test (PR A is refused by 1b, as intended, and just sits there); branch B is opened with base=A and contains only code. `pulls/B/files` returns no `.github/workflows/**` entry, `branchEditsCiDefinition` returns false, gate 1b passes — while B's `pull_request` CI run executed the merge ref of A+B, i.e. exactly the gutted ci.yml the gate exists to refuse. The panel itself does not share this blind spot (agent-review-panel.yml:455 diffs against `git merge-base origin/main HEAD`), so the two halves of the pipeline disagree about what "the branch changed" means, and 1b is the permissive one.

samples.summary: Off-by-one in the pagination loop: a PR with exactly 1000 changed files is refused as "more than 1000"
samples.evidence: `for (let page = 1; page <= 10; page++)` with `if (files.length < 100) return false;` at :192. For a PR with exactly 1000 changed files, page 10 returns a full 100-item page, the loop condition fails, and control reaches `throw new Error("more than 1000 changed files ...")` at :194 even though every file was enumerated and none matched. The gate then fails closed (ranBaseCiDefinition → false → exit 1), so a large but perfectly legitimate PR is permanently un-promotable with a message stating a false reason. The correct termination is to check for an empty page (or to compare a running total), not to rely on the last page being short.

samples.summary: A transient failure of the new pulls/files read strands the PR as a draft with no page and nothing to retry it
samples.evidence: `ranBaseCiDefinition` swallows ANY error from `branchEditsCiDefinition` — including a one-off 5xx/network failure from `gh api` — logs to stderr and returns false (:205-206). The gate array then makes `allOk` false and the process exits 1 (:255). The promote job treats exit 1 as success (agent-review-panel.yml:1539-1542, "leaving as draft") because the verdict line IS printed, so nothing pages. `gh api` is not retried here (contrast the `retries: 3` on the github-script gate at agent-review-panel.yml:183), and the promote job only re-runs on the next CI-green push — which, for a finished PR, never comes. This is the exact "a PR that should have merged would sit as a draft forever" failure the promote job's own header comment (agent-review-panel.yml:1454-1461) says the design exists to prevent; the delta adds a new unretried read on that path.

samples.summary: The hand-off comment asserts more to the human reviewer than gate 1b verified
samples.evidence: Lines 320-322 tell the accountable human signer "the branch changes no workflow definition, so that run executed the CI file on `main` rather than one the branch supplied." Two ways that is untrue of what was checked: (a) the file list is the diff against the PR's base, not `main` (see the stacked-PR finding), and (b) the gate only covers `.github/workflows/` and `.github/actions/` (CI_DEFINING_PREFIXES, :175), while what CI actually executes is largely branch-supplied — the `verify:self`/`verify:integration` npm scripts in package.json, vitest/jest configs, etc. A branch that empties those produces the same green run at the same path with no workflow file touched, and this comment tells the reviewer that possibility was excluded. A false assurance in the one artifact the human reads is worse than no assurance; the sentence should state the narrow fact ("changes no file under .github/workflows or .github/actions").

samples.summary: Gates 1 and 1b can evaluate two different commits: gate 1 pins headRefOid, gate 1b reads the PR's file list live
samples.evidence: `ciGate = ciPassed(pr.headRefOid)` (:166) is fixed to the SHA snapshotted at :122, but `ranBaseCiDefinition(prNumber)` (:210) queries `pulls/{n}/files`, which reflects whatever the head is at the moment of the call. If a commit lands in that window, the two gates are answering about different trees: a head that carried a workflow edit can supply the green run gate 1 reads, while the newer head supplies the clean file list gate 1b reads, and the composite conclusion ("this green run came from main's CI definition") holds for neither. Narrow race, but it is the exact composition the gate pair is supposed to make sound; pinning the file list to `pr.headRefOid` (e.g. comparing against the base via a SHA-scoped compare endpoint) would remove it.

samples.summary: The staged `trigger-shape` canary lands in the `noop` concurrency group with cancel-in-progress, so it can be CANCELLED rather than red — the silence it exists to break
samples.evidence: The patch adds `trigger-shape` as a plain job of agent-review-panel.yml, which is governed by the workflow-level `concurrency` at .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:115-118. That group's suffix evaluates to `noop` for precisely the payloads the canary fires on (`path != '.github/workflows/ci.yml'`, which includes an empty path), and `cancel-in-progress: true`. So on the mass-failure the canary is designed for — `workflow_run.path` stops being populated, every CI run refused — successive refused events for the same head repo+branch land in one group and each cancels the previous one in progress. A cancelled job is not a failed job (the panel's own `stalled` net is `!cancelled()`, per the comment at :101-102), so the canary can be silenced by the very condition it is meant to page on. It needs its own concurrency group (or none) rather than inheriting the noop one.

samples.summary: The staged canary's `if:` has no `github.event.action` clause, so one bad CI run produces two failing jobs
samples.evidence: Unlike `gate` (agent-review-panel.yml:164-169), which admits only `requested` or a re-run attempt, the patch's `trigger-shape` gates solely on pipeline-enabled + same-repo + path. The workflow subscribes to both `requested` and `completed`, so a single refused CI run fires the canary twice (two red runs, two error annotations) for one cause. Harmless but doubles the noise of the failure mode the job reports.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. `branchEditsCiDefinition` (scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:181-195) reads `repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/${number}/files` at line 183, which is the PR's diff against ITS OWN base ref, while the gate's stated and user-reported invariant is about main's CI definition (mark-ready.mjs:16-29, :238, :320-322). The PR metadata fetch at :122-128 never requests `baseRefName`, and no base-branch constraint exists anywhere on the promote path: the promote job (.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1453-1465, :1508) gates only on CI conclusion and panel blocked-status and forwards just the PR number. A repo-wide grep for baseRefName/base.ref/default_branch turns up nothing on this path. The panel by contrast diffs against `git merge-base origin/main HEAD` (agent-review-panel.yml:455, :459, :479), confirming the two halves disagree with 1b as the permissive one. The path is reachable: `agent:managed` human PRs ride the promote path unrestricted per the script's own comment (:28-29), and scripts/design-pr.mjs:385 accepts an arbitrary `--base`, so a PR stacked on a branch that edits `.github/workflows/**` returns no workflow entry from `pulls/N/files`, passes 1b, and is auto-promoted on a CI run that executed the merge ref's branch-supplied ci.yml. Existing tests (mark-ready.test.mjs:262-290) only cover the same-base case, so nothing guards it. This is a wrong condition / broken invariant in my lane, not merely a security concern, since a benign stacked PR triggers the same false "CI ran main's definition" claim.

searchedFor: grep for prior uses of workflow_run payload fields in workflows
finding.summary: The whole agent pipeline is now conditioned on `github.event.workflow_run.path`, a payload field nothing in the repo previously read and nothing validates — an empty/absent value disables panel, fixer and CI report with no page
finding.evidence: `grep` over `.github/` shows `github.event.workflow_run.path` appears only in the lines this diff adds (agent-review-panel.yml:117,166; agent-iterate-ci.yml:54; ci-report.yml:56); it is a first use. The tests exercise the clause only against synthetic PATH values injected into `new Function` (checks.test.mjs:183-218), never against a real payload. If the field is ever missing or differently populated (e.g. for the `requested` action, or a run created before a rename), the expression is false everywhere at once: the panel gate skips, the concurrency suffix resolves to 'noop', `stalled` is gated on `gate.outputs.managed` and therefore also skips, and no human is told. A single unverified field with a fail-silent blast radius over the whole loop.

verdict.reason: The cited code is present as described (path clauses at agent-review-panel.yml:117,166; agent-iterate-ci.yml:54; ci-report.yml:56, all gating by skipping, and no trigger-shape canary landed), but it is not a blocking correctness defect. The asserted failure requires a hypothetical GitHub payload regression: `workflow_run.path` is a documented member of the same payload object whose `run_attempt`, `conclusion`, `head_repository.full_name` and `head_branch` fields these very clauses already depend on (agent-review-panel.yml:164-169, agent-iterate-ci.yml:52-56); nothing in the repo evidences an empty or differently-shaped `path`, and field novelty is not evidence the condition is wrong for real payloads. The only divergence reachable today — a renamed ci.yml or a second file claiming `name: CI` — is precisely what the clause exists to refuse, and such PRs are already un-automated by design (mark-ready.mjs:20-21,173-175 CI_DEFINING_PREFIXES; harness-engineering.md:1911-1921). What remains is an observability gap for an upstream payload change, explicitly documented with a staged canary (checks.mjs:54-64, harness-engineering.md:1932-1944, docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-trigger-shape.patch), not a wrong condition, missing null guard, dropped await, or data-loss path — i.e. the 'defensive/unreachable branch, input outside the feature's stated range' category, minor at most under the Correctness rubric.
